power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

stat_p_exact.title: Exact P-Values
stat_p_exact.summary_text: We found no imprecise *p* values, *p*-values of exactly zero or impossible *p* values out of 3 detected.

table.formatted: Cases with biTP53 showed substantially greater genomic complexity than other AMLs, with more WGS-detected SVs and CNAs (Figures <ref type="figure" target="#fig_3">5B-C</ref>, Figures <ref type="figure" target="#fig_0">S4-S10</ref>), supporting the view that CK in AML largely serves as a surrogate marker of biTP53. <ref type="bibr" target="#b44">45,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b46">[47]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b47">[48]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b48">[49]</ref> Compared with SoC-determined CK cases lacking a TP53 mutation, biTP53 cases had markedly more chromosomal aberrations by WGS (median 20 vs 3; p<0.001, Mann-Whitney U-test; Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_3">5B</ref>).
table.header: WGS refines TP53 allelic state determination and assessment of complex karyotype
table.expanded: Cases with biTP53 showed substantially greater genomic complexity than other AMLs, with more WGS-detected SVs and CNAs (Figures 5B-C, Figures S4-S10), supporting the view that CK in AML largely serves as a surrogate marker of biTP53. 45, [47] [48] [49] Compared with SoC-determined CK cases lacking a TP53 mutation, biTP53 cases had markedly more chromosomal aberrations by WGS (median 20 vs 3; p<0.001, Mann-Whitney U-test; Figure 5B).

table.formatted: Points represent individual cases; statistical significance was assessed using a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (*** P < 0.001).

ownership.dep_description: A set of command line tools (in Java) for manipulating high-throughput sequencing (HTS) data and formats such as SAM/BAM/CRAM and VCF.
ownership.context: Variant liftover (for gene panel and WES variants in the hg19 reference), normalization, and matching between WGS and SoC pipelines were performed using Picard (v2.22.1; https://github.com/broadinstitute/picard), BCFtools 38 (v1.11) and a custom Python script.
